page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, running two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, along with AES cryptography and BMI2 bit manipulation instructions. The system includes 35 MB of L3 cache, a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and operates without bundled local storage or dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate typical characteristics of an older enterprise architecture. Compute benchmarks show moderate PassMark CPU scores of 6,967.25, while stress-ng single-core (1,105.79) and multi-core (5,885.34) reflect bottom-quartile throughput. Geekbench scoring aligns with this profile, reporting 969.0 for single-core and 3,819.0 for multi-core tests. Single-threaded compression tasks register low rates, including 19.1 GB/sec in gzip and 7.35 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression.

Memory throughput exhibits distinct tiers depending on block size: cached 16 KB read speeds register at 328.36 GB/sec, whereas uncached 256 MB reads reach 41.01 GB/sec and writes achieve 35.87 GB/sec. Operational metrics include 5.58 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 5.86 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based LLM inference achieves 457.92 prompt tokens per second on small 135M models, but drops to 5.25 tokens per second for medium 7B model generation.

Given its 1:8 core-to-memory allocation, ecs.r5.2xlarge prioritizes memory footprint over raw execution speed. It serves workloads constrained primarily by RAM capacity rather than compute throughput, including in-memory caching systems, distributed memory caches, background ETL buffers, and staging database instances that do not require high network bandwidth or fast local NVMe disks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.2xlarge is a memory-optimized KVM instance featuring 8 vCPUs (4 physical cores) on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz and 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The instance lacks local storage and discrete GPUs, relying on a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Compute performance is modest, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 3,819.0 and a PassMark CPU rating of 6,967.25. Memory bandwidth reaches 41.01 GB/sec for uncached large reads and 35.87 GB/sec for writes, alongside a Redis SET throughput of 5.58 million operations per second. While instruction extensions like AVX-512 are present, CPU-heavy tasks such as compression and medium-model LLM execution show limited throughput. The configuration provides a cost-effective memory density tailored for in-memory caching, ETL buffers, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
